# linux_local_forward (Data Source)

Establishes SSH local port forwarding through the connection of the provider.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "linux_local_forward" "remote" {
  remote_host = "127.0.0.1"
  remote_port = 3306
  local_host  = "127.0.0.1"
  local_port  = 3306
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `remote_host` (String) Host that the SSH server forwards connections to, resolved from the SSH server.
- `remote_port` (Number) Port that the SSH server forwards connections to.

### Optional

- `local_host` (String) Local address to listen on. The default, `0.0.0.0`, accepts connections on every network interface.
- `local_port` (Number) Local port to listen on. The default, `0`, picks a random free port.
- `provider_override` (Block List, Max: 1) SSH connection settings used by this object instead of the provider configuration, as a workaround for dynamic providers. It accepts the same arguments as the provider plus an `id`, which identifies the connection in the connection pool and for locking. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--provider_override))

### Read-Only

- `host` (String) Local address that is listening for connections. It equals `local_host`.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `port` (Number) Local port that is listening for connections. It equals `local_port`, or the port that was picked when `local_port` is `0`.

<a id="nestedblock--provider_override"></a>
### Nested Schema for `provider_override`

Required:

- `id` (String) Connection instance ID for locking purpose when defined in resource/datasource

Optional:

- `agent` (Boolean) Set to `false` to disable using ssh-agent to authenticate.
- `agent_identity` (String) The preferred identity from the ssh agent for authentication.
- `bastion_certificate` (String) The contents of a signed CA Certificate. The certificate argument must be used in conjunction with a `bastion_private_key`. These can be loaded from a file on disk using the the `file` function.
- `bastion_host` (String) Setting this enables the bastion Host connection. This host will be connected to first, and then the `host` connection will be made from there.
- `bastion_host_key` (String) The public key from the remote host or the signing CA, used to verify the host connection. Defaults to the value of the `host_key` field.
- `bastion_password` (String, Sensitive) The password we should use for the bastion host. Defaults to the value of the `password` field.
- `bastion_port` (Number) The port to use connect to the bastion host. Defaults to the value of the `port` field.
- `bastion_private_key` (String, Sensitive) The contents of an SSH key file to use for the bastion host. These can be loaded from a file on disk using the `file` function. Defaults to the value of the `private_key` field.
- `bastion_user` (String) The user for the connection to the bastion host. Defaults to the value of the `user` field.
- `certificate` (String) The contents of a signed CA Certificate. The certificate argument must be used in conjunction with a `private_key`. These can be loaded from a file on disk using the the `file` function.
- `host` (String) The address of the resource to connect to.
- `host_key` (String) The public key from the remote host or the signing CA, used to verify the connection.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password we should use for the connection.
- `port` (Number) The port to connect to. Defaults to `22`.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) The contents of an SSH key to use for the connection. These can be loaded from a file on disk using the `file` function. This takes preference over the `password` if provided.
- `script_path` (String) The path used to copy scripts meant for remote execution.
- `timeout` (String) The timeout to wait for the connection to become available. Should be provided as a string like `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to 5 minutes.
- `user` (String) The user that we should use for the connection. Defaults to `root`.
